findings.claim: The angular coordinate change is O(epsilon)-close in derivative to the Kerr map, its angular Jacobian extends continuously at the Cauchy horizon in old compactified coordinates, and continuous S-tangent tensors transfer to the new coordinates; Theorem 16.14 invokes these assertions.
findings.suspect_step: Treating the nondecaying rigid Kerr rotation and its stereographic component derivative as an integrable decaying coefficient; using D Psi at the old point instead of the image point in chart compatibility.

counterexample.assumptions: Exact Kerr compared with itself, so every initial-data difference and all weighted norms vanish. Strict 0<a<M; any fixed allowed delta>0, large N, small epsilon and corresponding sufficiently negative u_f. Start sequences late enough for u+v>=C_R and compactifying-coordinate formula. Equator in both specified chart interiors; no endpoint or chart-boundary exception.
counterexample.stated_result: Jacobian values at the same old angle become Cauchy with bound C*abs(v_n^(-2delta)-w_n^(-2delta))^(1/2)
counterexample.actual_result: J_K(v_n)=I, J_K(w_n)=-I, gap 2; map values x and -x, whereas both old sequences converge to (u,0,x)
counterexample.complete_check: The positive tail difference is <v_n^(-2delta) and tends to zero. Even if the printed stereographic forced equation defines a different map, the asserted componentwise O(epsilon) Jacobian closeness with C epsilon<1/2 gives a gap >1, contradicting the simultaneously asserted continuity. No epsilon-to-zero limit with varying u_f is required.
counterexample.tensor_check: f=sin(theta_*)cos(phi_*)=2x/(1+x^2+y^2) is globally smooth, old-coordinate v independent. Under the intended Kerr map its new-coordinate equatorial values at phi_CH=0 are cos(3v), hence +1/-1. If scalar rank zero is excluded, use f times the unit round metric.
counterexample.shift_check: b_K=B J0 x; B->3 and D_x b_K->3J0. A.47 controls special scalar components, not all stereographic derivatives. Integral of the absolute nonzero limiting off-diagonal component diverges.
counterexample.covariance_check: Correct transformed forcing uses D Psi(F(x)); printed equation uses D Psi(x). Granting the r_- correction, residual for Kerr is (B-3)(R(-3v)-I)J0 x. At equator B=(12/5)/(r^3+9r/25+18/25)<3 for all r>1/5; thus residual is nonzero at legitimate finite late v with nonidentity rotation. The sample r=1/2, R=-I gives (0,54/41), only an illustrative algebra substitution.

counterevidence: Exact Kerr is smoothly extendible in its regular rotating coordinates; no physical theorem counterexample is asserted
Interior rotation determinant is 1 and all finite-time maps are regular
Axisymmetry can cancel rotations in the metric even though generic tensors fail to extend
Local polar Jacobian expressions do not remove the unbounded azimuthal phase or supply the required global stereographic limit
The different completion spaces can be abstractly homeomorphic; the identity on their common interior is the transition that fails to extend
findings.impact: Invalid core derivation in the reviewed 2017 v1: Proposition 16.11 and Corollary 16.13 are explicitly used by Theorem 16.14 and the main C0 extension argument. A replacement nonlinear proof is needed. Does not establish failure of the main geometric conclusion or of the unexamined 2025 journal text.

repair.statement: Limited lemma: on S2, for b(v)=omega V+q(v) with V a rigid rotation and integral ||q(v)||_C1 finite, the flow conjugated by the inverse rigid rotation converges in C1 to a C1 diffeomorphism.
repair.verification: Complete flow/variational-equation proof in report: integrable vector field gives uniform Cauchy displacement, Gronwall bounds derivatives and inverse derivatives, integrable derivative tail gives C1 convergence and compactness gives surjectivity.
repair.remaining: Full intrinsic coordinate construction, the exact mixed-norm estimates and nonlinear transformed-metric continuity not repaired. Need revisions to the implicated Section 16 claims.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Root directly read source lines9631-9750 and actually viewed original page181: (16.55) compares derivatives at different advanced times and the same old angular point, and explicitly bounds their difference by a vanishing power tail. The stated extension is in the old compactified coordinates. Theorem16.14 explicitly invokes the tensor-transfer corollary. This is not a misreading of a comparison along the rotating flow.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: Exact subextremal Kerr with M1,a3/5 gives r-=1/5,r+=9/5,omega-=3 and compactification rate4; all differences from Kerr and weighted error norms vanish. Fix allowed delta,N,epsilon,u_f and take sufficiently late v_n=2pi n/3,w_n=(2pi n+pi)/3 at an equatorial point in both charts. The intended stereographic Kerr Jacobian alternates I and -I, gap2, while both compactified times converge to0 and the printed tail tends0. Even if the forced printed map differs from exact Kerr, its asserted uniform O(epsilon) Jacobian closeness for Cepsilon<1/2 contradicts simultaneous continuity. The auxiliary's actual exact rational calculation PID51476 exit0 confirms omega3,rate4,B(1/2)=96/41 and chart residual54/41.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The actual Kerr geometry extends smoothly in regular rotating coordinates. Axisymmetry can cancel rotation in its metric, but a generic old-coordinate continuous scalar sin(theta)cos(phi), or that scalar times the round metric, oscillates in the new coordinates. Stereographic D_x b_K tends3J0, so the claimed integrability is not supplied by the special polar component estimate A.47. Correct chart covariance uses D Psi at F(x), not x. The limited relative-flow lemma is valid when the rotation-subtracted remainder has integrable C1 norm, by uniform flow/variational bounds. It does not repair the nonlinear coordinate and metric proof.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the explicit core coordinate-continuity derivation in the bound2017v1; no counterexample to the geometric C0 theorem or unexamined2025 journal text. Phase normalization is not an excluded hypothesis: v0=10pi k/3 can satisfy both the printed and squared-denominator versions, so that typo is not a new counted problem.

findings.claim: Smooth strictly decreasing u and strictly increasing v on the spacelike initial curve suffice for local nonsingular double-null coordinates solving the eikonal equations.
findings.suspect_step: Strict monotonicity is treated as pointwise nonzero derivative.

counterexample.hypersurface: t=0, all S2, induced positive metric
counterexample.assumptions: Smooth injective regular curve, derivative (-3tau^2,1) never zero; smooth inverse parameter v; -tau^3 strictly decreasing, tau strictly increasing; radius positive; smooth isometric spacelike embedding.
counterexample.complete_check: At tau=0 all tangential derivatives of u vanish. Eikonal equation gives -(N u)^2+|d_Sigma u|^2=0, hence N u=0 and full du=0. Coordinate differentials cannot vanish. Therefore the stated conclusion fails at that sphere.

counterevidence: A stronger reading meaning derivatives strictly signed excludes the example, but is an additional hypothesis
Main initial data u=C_R-tau, v=tau have derivatives -1 and 1; n tau=(Phi-|w|^2)^(-1/2)>0
findings.impact: Peripheral/local overstatement; no demonstrated damage to the main-data invocation.

repair.statement: Require partial_tau u<0 and partial_tau v>0 pointwise, with the existing smooth spacelike hypotheses.
repair.verification: Then tangential normal derivatives nu,nv are nonzero; chosen eikonal normal roots Nu,Nv are nonzero; the derivative of the eikonal relation with respect to the normal first derivative is -2Nu or -2Nv, so the ordinary smooth noncharacteristic local construction applies. Compactness gives a common small sphere neighborhood.
repair.scope: Local construction only, no additional global theorem.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Proposition2.1 assumes smooth strict monotonicity of the initial scalar coordinate functions; this does not force their derivatives to be nonzero at every point.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: In the Minkowski annulus -dt^2+d tau^2+(2+tau)^2dOmega^2, t0 is spacelike. The parameter curve (-tau^3,tau) is smooth, injective and regular with derivative(-3tau^2,1); its first coordinate is strictly decreasing. At tau0 all tangential derivatives of u vanish, so the eikonal equation forces its normal derivative0 as well, leaving du0 and excluding a coordinate chart.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Requiring partial_tau u<0 and partial_tau v>0 ensures nonzero normal eikonal roots and the standard local noncharacteristic construction. The actual main data u=C_R-tau,v=tau already have derivatives-1,+1. This is a local repair, not a new global existence proof.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for a local overbroad hypothesis, with no demonstrated harm to the actual main-data application.
